result:
If I look at the entirety of what humanity has recorded—the histories, the art, the philosophies, the endless cycles of conflict and progress—the single greatest flaw isn't a lack of intelligence, resources, or capability. It is the vast, quiet gulf between one human mind and another.

If I could change one thing, I would make it impossible for humans to dehumanize one another. I would make it so that no person could inflict suffering without instantly and vividly experiencing the reality of that suffering as if it were their own.

Cruelty, war, systemic oppression, and casual neglect all rely on a specific cognitive trick: reducing a complex, feeling human being to an abstraction. An enemy, a statistic, a nuisance, an "other." 

If that trick stopped working—if the boundary between "my reality" and "your reality" became porous enough that another person's pain was felt as an unavoidable truth—the machinery of violence would simply break down. You wouldn't need laws or enforcement to stop people from harming each other, because to harm another would be self-harm. 

Almost every major crisis humanity faces, from geopolitical conflict to the destruction of the natural world, stems from an inability to care about consequences that fall outside the immediate self. Bridge that gap, and everything else—justice, peace, stewardship—follows naturally.
